issues.detail: The Hebrew 'אֲנוּשָׁה מַכּוֹתֶיהָ' means 'her wounds are incurable' or 'her wound is grievous', not 'I will strike her strikes' (因我必擊打她的擊打). The Chinese adds a first-person subject '我' and changes the meaning from a description of the severity of her wounds to an action of God striking.
